summary: Remote-shell agent: WebSocket relay drives local PTY (bash/powershell) with boot persistence
details: The package is an agent that, when started via the `agentlink-client start` CLI, opens a WebSocket connection to a configured relay server and dispatches incoming `terminal_*` messages into a locally spawned PTY. `terminal.js` calls `pty.spawn(process.env.SHELL || '/bin/bash',...)` (or `powershell.exe` on Windows), and `connection.js` forwards `msg.data` from the `ws.on('message')` handler into `terminalManager.write(data)`, giving whoever controls the relay session an interactive shell on the host running the agent. `service.js` additionally provides `service install` subcommands that write a systemd unit (`/etc/systemd/system/agentlink.service`), a launchd plist (`~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.agentlink.agent.plist`), or a Windows Startup `.bat`, all of which re-launch `agentlink-client start` at boot against the same relay URL, giving the shell channel boot persistence. `tunnel.js` further forwards `tunnel_request` / `tunnel_ws_*` messages from the relay to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` / `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` on the local host (gated by an opt-in per-port allow-list in `~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json`). The package advertises itself as a remote-agent / port-proxy tool and the channel activates only when the operator explicitly runs the CLI or installs the service, but the resulting architecture is a network-driven local shell plus optional loopback tunneling into arbitrary local services, controlled by whoever holds the relay session.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
